results.reader_what: The study combines interactive horizon scanning with NEST layers to make weak signals more usable for organisational decision-making.

recovered_sources.title: The future of business in Visegrad region

verification.verification_note: The full article explicitly combines macro and micro scenario methods, discusses methodological limitations and says the approach can be replicated elsewhere.

admission.reason: The article presents and reflects on a replicable two-level scenario design that combines macro quantitative and micro expert-based foresight.

metadata_correction.reason: Springer metadata corrects the journal and gives the exact publication date.

results.reader_what: The study combines macro quantitative scenarios with company-level expert workshops in a replicable business-foresight design.
results.reader_why: Combining scales can connect structural economic change with firm-level strategic uncertainty.
results.reader_more: The paper builds Visegrad macro scenarios from quantitative indicators and micro scenarios through expert workshops using intuitive-logic axes. It presents the combined design as readily replicable and uses the macro–micro combination to curb limitations of the scenario-axes technique. The contribution adapts established methods rather than inventing scenario planning from scratch.

deep_analysis.research_question: How can macroeconomic and company-level foresight be combined to explore business futures in the Visegrad region?
deep_analysis.main_finding: A combined macro quantitative and micro expert-scenario design links regional structural futures with firm-level strategic scenarios.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Macro indicator analysis combined with expert-based scenario workshops and a two-axis/four-quadrant intuitive-logic design.
deep_analysis.qualification: The approach combines established scenario techniques and was demonstrated in Visegrad business cases; it is an adaptation, not a wholly new scenario method.
deep_analysis.radar_relevance: The explicit, replicable integration of two analytical levels is a material reusable scenario-method contribution qualifying for Strand B.

claims.qualification: The approach combines established scenario techniques and was demonstrated in Visegrad business cases; it is an adaptation, not a wholly new scenario method.
claims.text: The paper integrates macro quantitative scenarios with micro expert workshops into a replicable two-level business foresight design.
